'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Assassination of Luca Attanasio]]
**Six gunmen open fire on a [[World Food Programme]] convoy in [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], killing [[government of Italy|Italian]] ambassador [[Luca Attanasio]], a [[Carabinieri|carabiniere]] and their driver. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/22/italian-ambassador-to-dr-congo-dies-in-attack-un-convoy-luca-attanasio (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Four female development workers are killed and their driver wounded when gunmen open fire on their vehicle in [[Mir Ali, Pakistan|Mira Ali]], [[North Waziristan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/22/pakistan-women-aid-workers-shot-dead-by-assailants (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Rwanda]]n opposition [[politics of Rwanda|politician]] [[Seif Bamporiki]] is killed in his car by a single bullet fired by a gunman in [[Cape Town]], [[South Africa]], where he lived in [[exile]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-56119088 (BBC News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cinema]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in New York City]]
**[[New York (state)|New York]] [[Governor of New York|Governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] announces that movie theatres in [[New York City]] can reopen with 25% capacity on March 5, in line with rules currently in place for locations in the rest of the state. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/02/22/movie-theaters-in-new-york-city-can-open-in-march-at-25percent-capacity.html (CNBC)]
*French [[electronic music]] duo [[Daft Punk]] announce their split after 28 years. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/22/arts/music/daft-punk-breakup.html (''The New York Times'')] 

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
*****[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|British Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] announces a new four-step plan for easing [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] restrictions in [[England]], starting with the reopening of schools on March 8 and the lifting of the [[stay-at-home order]] on March 29. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-02-23/boris-johnson-unveils-roadmap-for-ending-englands-covid-lockdown/13181348 (ABC Australia)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]], [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
*****Students in P1 to P3 return to school in [[Scotland]] for the first time since the [[Christmas]] holiday as part of a phased school reopening. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-56152201 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[Government of France|French authorities]] announce that 90% of residents in the southeastern region of [[Alpes-Maritimes]], which includes [[Nice]], will be placed under a weekend lockdown for the next two weeks following an increase in the number of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/02/22/covid-19-france-imposes-weekend-lockdown-on-southeastern-region (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]], [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
****Elementary students and pre-school children in more than half of Germany's 16 [[States of Germany|states]] return to schools and kindergartens in the first major easing of restrictions since December. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/germany-reopens-schools-amid-fears-pandemic-rebound-76039960 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] extends their ban on non-essential travel between [[Regions of Italy|regions]] with the exception of business trips and emergencies until March 27 due to the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] infections. [https://www.brusselstimes.com/news/world-all-news/156271/italy-extends-ban-on-travel-between-regions/ (''The Brussels Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****The [[White House]] orders [[Flag of the United States|United States flags]] to fly at [[half-staff]] for the next five days in order to honor those who have died from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/biden-covid-announcement-flag-us-deaths-b1805832.html (''The Independent'')]
****The [[United States]] surpasses 500,000 deaths from COVID-19, just five weeks after the country passed 400,000 deaths. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-19-deaths-in-us-top-500000/ (CBS News)] [https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2021/02/22/969494791/a-loss-to-the-whole-society-u-s-covid-19-death-toll-reaches-500-000 (NPR)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Mexico]]
*****[[Mexico]] receives the first shipment of 200,000 doses of [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine. [https://www.voanews.com/covid-19-pandemic/mexico-receives-first-shipment-russian-vaccine-fight-covid-19 (VOA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maharashtra]]
*****[[Maharashtra]] imposes a ban on all political, social, and religious gatherings, as well as all processions and public demonstrations in order to reduce the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/trends/maharashtra-bans-gatherings-cm-thackeray-warns-of-new-lockdown-as-covid-19-cases-spike/story/431928.html (''Business Today'')]
****[[India]] surpasses 11 million cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], becoming the second country to do so after the [[United States]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/indias-covid-19-tally-over-11-million-death-toll-at-156385-101613966685580.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines]]
*****The [[Philippines]] approves the emergency use of the [[Sinovac Biotech]] [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for non-[[healthcare workers]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-22/philippines-clears-china-s-sinovac-vaccine-for-emergency-use (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Thailand]]
*****[[Thailand]]'s Food and Drug Administration grants emergency use authorization for the [[Sinovac Biotech]] [[CoronaVac]] vaccine. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-thailand-idUSL4N2KS37D (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Chief Executive of Hong Kong|Chief Executive]] [[Carrie Lam]] and other [[Government of Hong Kong|government]] officials receive their first doses of the [[Sinovac Biotech]] [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] as [[Hong Kong]] begins its [[vaccination]] campaign. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/hong-kong-leader-carrie-lam-and-top-officials-to-get-covid-19-vaccine-on-monday (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] surpasses 80,000 cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [http://www.adaderana.lk/news/71776/sri-lankas-covid-19-cases-top-80000 (Ada Derana)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Somalia]]
***[[Somalia]] closes all schools and universities for the next two weeks due to an increase in the number of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/covid-19-schools-shut-for-2-weeks-in-somalia/2153590 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[GlaxoSmithKline]] and [[Sanofi]] begins new clinical trial of their protein-based [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] candidate and aim to reach the final testing stage in the second quarter after setback last year. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/02/22/gsk-sanofi-begin-new-covid-19-vaccine-trial-after-setback-last-year.html (CNBC)]
**[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***The [[Vatican Press Office]] announces that all journalists to accompany [[Pope Francis]] on his March trip to [[Iraq]] must receive a [[Deployment of COVID-19 vaccines|Covid vaccination]]. [[International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis|Certificates of vaccination]] are required for reporters seeking press [[Credential|credential]]s for the trip. [https://www.catholicculture.org/news/headlines/index.cfm?storyid=49877 (Catholic Culture)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Uyghur genocide]], [[Canada–China relations]]
**[[Canada]]'s [[House of Commons of Canada|House of Commons]] approves a motion by 266 to zero votes, formally recognizing that China is committing [[genocide]] against its [[Islam in China|Muslim]] [[Uyghurs|Uyghur]] [[minorities in China|minority]] in [[Xinjiang]]. However, [[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] and most of his [[29th Canadian Ministry|Cabinet]] did not participate in the vote. An amendment to the bill also calls for the [[2022 Winter Olympics]] to be moved from [[Beijing]] if the genocide continues. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-parliament-declares-china-is-conducting-genocide-against-its-muslim/ (''The Globe and Mail'')]
*[[Prime Minister of Fiji|Fijian Prime Minister]] [[Frank Bainimarama]] urges the leaders of the [[Federated States of Micronesia]], the [[Marshall Islands]], [[Nauru]], [[Kiribati]], and [[Palau]] to reconsider their decision of leaving the [[Pacific Islands Forum]] and says that this is an opportunity to fight climate change. Bainimarama also invites [[U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] to the next forum meeting in August. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/436911/fiji-urges-micronesia-to-rethink-plans-to-leave-forum (RNZ)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Cannabis in the United States]]
**[[Cannabis in New Jersey]]
***Enabling legislation for [[2020 New Jersey Public Question 1|Public Question 1]] is signed into law by [[Governor of New Jersey|Governor]] [[Phil Murphy]], making [[New Jersey]] the [[Legality of cannabis by U.S. jurisdiction|14th state to legalize recreational cannabis]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/new-jersey-governor-signs-laws-legalize-marijuana-use-decriminalize-possession-n1258534 (NBC News)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**A [[general strike]] begins in [[Myanmar]] despite warnings by the [[Tatmadaw]] that further confrontations could cost lives. [https://www.dw.com/en/myanmar-general-strike-goes-ahead-despite-threats/a-56646718 (DW)]<!-- See the talk page for an explanation of this news item. -->
*[[Gambling in Australia]]
**The [[Victoria State Government]] establishes a [[royal commission]] into [[Crown Melbourne]] after [[New South Wales]] revoked [[Crown Resorts]]' gambling license over [[money laundering]] concerns. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/feb/22/victoria-to-establish-royal-commission-into-melbournes-crown-casino (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Personal and business legal affairs of Donald Trump]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United States|United States Supreme Court]], by a 7–2 vote, declines to block the [[subpoena]] of [[Manhattan]] [[New York County District Attorney|District Attorney]] [[Cyrus Vance Jr.]] for former President [[Donald Trump]]'s financial records, including his [[Tax returns of Donald Trump|tax returns]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/02/22/politics/supreme-court-trump-taxes-vance/index.html (CNN)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 Russian protests]], [[2020–21 NHL season]]
**In [[ice hockey]], [[New York Rangers]] [[Winger (ice hockey)|winger]] [[Artemi Panarin]] takes a personal leave of absence after the Russian [[Tabloid (newspaper format)|tabloid]] [[Komsomolskaya Pravda]] publishes a story in which former [[Kontinental Hockey League]] coach [[Andrei Nazarov]] accuses him of sexually assaulting a 18-year old [[Latvians|Latvian]] woman in [[Riga]]. The team releases a statement calling the allegations against Panarin a “intimidation tactic” against him after speaking out against “recent political events”, most notably being critical of [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] and expressing his support for [[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|Russian opposition leader]] [[Alexei Navalny]], who was detained upon return to [[Russia]] from [[Germany]]. [https://www.axios.com/artemi-panarin-navalny-putin-78b80d4a-bafd-460c-bb9d-a7678b92f51e.html (Axios)] [https://amp.theguardian.com/sport/2021/feb/22/artemi-panarin-new-york-rangers-leave-putin-navalny-nhl (''The Guardian'')]
